heading: Reactor configuration
reported_value: Confined APGD: stainless-steel (310S) cathode pin and anode plate; cathode and discharge region inside a Macor ceramic tube, inner radius 2.5 mm; ~1 mm groove in cathode for gas inlet (vortex); anode 22 mm from cathode tip with central gas exit
evidence_excerpt_or_description: The cathode and the discharge region are fully surrounded by a tube made of Macor machinable high temperature ceramic, with an inner radius of 2.5 mm.

heading: Electricity supply
reported_value: Technix high-voltage DC supply, up to 30 kV and 40 mA
evidence_excerpt_or_description: A high voltage Technix DC power supply capable of supplying up to 30 kV and 40 mA is used to deliver the power to the plasma.
basis_and_boundary: Lab DC supply; wall power not reported

heading: Electricity supply
reported_value: 300 kOhm ballast resistor; voltage pre-set to 30 kV, drops after ignition to ~10-15 kV read from the supply
evidence_excerpt_or_description: The plasma is sustained in the glow regime by means of a 300 kOhm ballast resistor. The initial voltage has been pre-set each time to 30 kV, after which it drops once the plasma is ignited to a value that can be read directly from the power supply (around 10-15 kV, depending on the applied conditions).
basis_and_boundary: Ballast in series between supply and plasma
notes: Ballast I^2R (188-368 W) exceeds plasma power (97-145 W); see E043

heading: Electricity supply
reported_value: SEI = plasma power / total inlet flow; method for determining plasma power not stated; no point powers tabulated
evidence_excerpt_or_description: The energy costs are calculated based on the total conversions and specific energy input (SEI), which is defined as the ratio of plasma power over total gas flow rate.
basis_and_boundary: Plasma power (excludes ballast loss presumably); probably supply V minus I*R times I, not confirmed
uncertainty: Method unknown; whether ballast loss is excluded is inferred from C005 voltage consistency
notes: Authors themselves question power measurement in another APGD study (E026) BB 2026-11-26: confirmed the paper does not say whether plasma power excludes the ballast or how it was measured; exclusion remains a reviewer inference (C005 voltage check).

heading: Methods
reported_value: Liquid trap then Thermo Trace 1310 GC (TCD; calibrated CO2, CH4, N2, O2, CO, H2, C2H2, C2H4, C2H6); N2 internal standard added after reactor at 10% of inlet flow; one blank and three plasma measurements per condition
locator: Section 2.1, para 3; ESI pp. 1-2, Eqs. S.E1-S.E2
evidence_excerpt_or_description: N2 is used as internal standard to account for the effects of gas expansion and of condensation of liquid products on the measured concentrations, and is added to the gas mixture after the reactor.

heading: Operating conditions
reported_value: CO2/CH4 with 15, 25, 35% CH4; total flow 0.5, 1, 2 L/min; current 20-35 mA; atmospheric pressure
evidence_excerpt_or_description: The CO2, CH4 and total conversion are presented in Fig. 3, for different currents (a) and flow rates (b), at a CH4 fraction of 25 %, as well as for different CH4 fractions, at 35 mA & 1 L/min (c), and at 25 mA & 0.5 L/min (d).

heading: Operating conditions
locator: Section 3.2, Eq. (E5); ESI p. 3 Eq. S.E11

heading: Energy

basis_and_boundary: Per molecule of CH4+CO2 converted; plasma power

heading: System information
reported_value: Higher currents or lower flows overheated and damaged ceramic tube, cathode and resistor; CH4 > 35% gave unstable plasma due to carbon
evidence_excerpt_or_description: Higher currents or lower flow rates than shown here unfortunately resulted in overheating and damage of some reactor parts, like the ceramic tube, cathode and resistor.

heading: Performance
